vintage: 2026 socioeconomic groups for the land's players (landscape spec 3.1-3.2; groups.md, the sociology pass of the redesign). Model shares computed on EconomicLives seed 2026, 2025 cut. Compiled 2026-10-02.
note: Every adult alive in a year lands in exactly one group by the priority rule below, on PersonYear fields only. Thresholds are relative (a rank, a wealth group, the year's median earnings, the Social Security share), so the rule works in every year of the cut. Class is read from the source of income (Gilbert, Wright); within wage earners from household income rank (Pew); occupation is proxied by industry (office vs frontline, after Dingel & Neiman's teleworkable jobs). Generation and party are attributes of the players, not groups. Party (Tribe) is drawn independently of class in this model (groups.md 6.1).
rule: 2 employed and self-employed: Earned >= medEarn(Y) or WealthGroup >= 2: business owners; else gig & freelance
3 employee: IncomeRank >= pmcRank: PMC; IncomeRank < poorRank: working poor; government industry: public servants; office industry: office & knowledge workers; else frontline & trades workers
4 not employed, age >= retireAge or on Social Security: SS >= ssDependence x (SS + wages + business + capital income): Social Security retirees; else comfortable retirees
5 not employed, under retireAge, married at mid-year (MarriageLog: Start <= Y + 0.5 < End) to an employed spouse: the spouse's group, anchored on the spouse's industry (Erikson's dominance rule)
6 not employed otherwise: under youngAge: students & young adults; else out of work
children: the mother's player, else the father's; with neither: the 1% if WealthGroup 3, PMC if IncomeRank >= pmcRank, else out of work
medEarn(Y) = median Earned over adults with Employed && !SelfEmployed ($65.6K in 2025)

cells.note: A cell (group x anchor x party) is a player with at least minLines lines (1M adults), or with at least richMinLines lines holding at least richWealthShare of national net worth. Too small: place cells join their tier (tier:<id>) within the group, tier cells pool into the group's rest, a rest too small joins the group's largest cell; within a cell a D, R or I part that passes the test is its own player, the rest pool into one mixed (M) player or join the largest part.

groups.name: The 1%
groups.rule: WealthGroup == 3 (the top 1% of adults by net worth)
groups.where: The crown when they live on capital; the top of their industry's tallest tower when they work where named companies are (controllers); else a gold plinth on the rim.
groups.basis: Fed DFA top 1% of net worth [data]; Gilbert's capitalist class, 1% [v]; model: 31.3% of net worth, DFA 31% [data].

groups.name: Business owners
groups.rule: employed, self-employed, Earned >= the year's median earnings or WealthGroup >= 2
groups.where: Their industry's surplus as proprietors' income: a gold plinth on the rim at their industry's angle.
groups.basis: BLS: self-employed about 10% of employed (model 10.3% [data]); Census ABS about 6M employer firms [recalled]; Wright's small employers [recalled].

groups.name: Gig & freelance
groups.where: Their industry, as thin proprietors' income below the median wage: a gold plinth on the rim.
groups.basis: BLS CWS July 2023: independent contractors 7.4% of employed, 11.9M [v]; Pew 2021 platform work [recalled]; Standing's precariat [recalled].

groups.name: Professional-managerial class
groups.where: Their industry's compensation, top-fifth households: the rim's first row.
groups.basis: Pew 2023: 19% of adults in upper-income households [v]; Gilbert's upper middle class 14-15% [v]; Reeves 2017 [recalled]; Ehrenreich & Ehrenreich 1977 [recalled].

groups.name: Public servants
groups.rule: employee of federal or state & local government (after the PMC and working-poor rules)
groups.where: Federal or state & local compensation: the rim above the government floor.
groups.basis: Government about 14.6% of nonfarm payroll [recalled]; union density 32% public vs 6% private [recalled].

groups.name: Office & knowledge workers
groups.rule: employee in an office industry (banking, finance, insurance, real estate, legal, professional, education, hardware, software, internet, media & telecom)
groups.basis: Dingel & Neiman 2020: 37% of jobs teleworkable [recalled]; what is left of management and professional occupations after the PMC and the public sector.

groups.name: Frontline & trades workers
groups.where: Frontline-industry compensation: health, trade, hospitality, manufacturing, construction, transport.
groups.basis: Gilbert's working class 30% plus part of the lower middle [v]; the COVID-era essential workers [recalled].

groups.name: Working poor
groups.rule: employee, household IncomeRank < 0.30 (checked right after the PMC rule)
groups.where: Low wages in any industry, plus means-tested transfers: the rim's outer row.
groups.basis: BLS working poor about 4% of the labor force [recalled]; Gilbert's working poor 13-15% [v]; Pew lower-income 30% of adults [v].

groups.name: Comfortable retirees
groups.rule: not employed, 62+ or on Social Security, Social Security < half of cash income
groups.where: Capital (pensions, 401k, home equity) plus Social Security: the rim at finance's angle (pensions).
groups.basis: Retirees about 22-25% of adults [recalled]; less than half of their income from Social Security.

groups.name: Social Security retirees
groups.rule: not employed, 62+ or on Social Security, Social Security >= half of cash income
groups.where: Federal transfers (Social Security, Medicare): the rim above the federal wedge.
groups.basis: SSA: 39% of men and 44% of women among beneficiaries 65+ get half or more of their income from Social Security [v].

groups.name: Students & young adults
groups.rule: not employed, under 25, no employed spouse
groups.where: Education and family transfers (not modeled), means-tested transfers: the rim at education's angle (schools).
groups.basis: NCES: about 38-40% of 18-24s enrolled; employment-population ratio about 62% [recalled].

groups.name: Out of work
groups.rule: not employed otherwise (a non-employed spouse of an employed adult takes the spouse's group)
groups.where: The safety net: state & local and federal transfers: the rim above the state & local wedge.
groups.basis: Gilbert's underclass 10-12% [v], minus the homemakers the dominance rule assigns to their spouse's class; prime-age participation about 83.4% [recalled].

sources.text: Pew Research Center (May 2024), The State of the American Middle Class: lower 30 / middle 51 / upper 19 (2023)
BLS, Contingent and Alternative Employment Arrangements, July 2023: independent contractors 7.4% of employed, 11.9M
SSA Fact Sheet: among beneficiaries 65+, 39% of men and 44% of women get half or more of their income from Social Security
Gilbert's class model: capitalist 1, upper middle 14-15, middle 30, working 30, working poor 13-15, underclass 10-12
Erikson (1984), Social class of men, women and families, Sociology 18(4): the dominance rule
Dingel & Neiman (2020), How many jobs can be done at home?, Journal of Public Economics 189: about 37% of US jobs
